nota: PENDENTE (Sala, item 7) → achado na fonte primária, palavra por palavra: 'The greatest single disaster of the flood occurred at Vanport, Oreg., when a railroad fill serving as a dike broke at 4:15 p.m. on Sunday, May 30.' (USGS WSP 1080, 'Floods of May–June 1948 in Columbia River Basin', p. 9). O ano está no título e no cabeçalho de cada página; 30/05/1948 foi domingo (conferido). Quem libera a tela é o verificador-de-fatos, com o redator. Os 51 são da cheia inteira; em Vanport, 'at least 16'. 'Within an hour the town was completely destroyed.'

grafias_do_espelho: AT LEAST 51 DEAD · THE WHOLE 1948 FLOOD · USGS, 1949
38,500 HOMELESS · RED CROSS, IN USGS 1949 (um número só, com o dono)
texto_aprovado: At Vanport, a railroad embankment was doing the work of a dike. It broke on a Sunday afternoon, and within an hour, by the US Geological Survey's account, the town was completely destroyed. Across the whole flood, the same report counts at least 51 people dead, and tens of thousands out of their homes.
